# Pixel

> Pixel is a local code index for AI coding agents: a single CLI (`pixel`) for macOS and Linux that answers repository questions (search, symbols, callers, task scope, Git history) from an index in `.pixel/`, so the agent reads less and edits with its blast radius known. The index stays on your machine, and there is no telemetry beyond an optional release check; only Git remotes, the optional `pixel classify` and `pixel web-search`, a one-time embedding model download, and a release check throttled to at most once per day use the network. Answers carry truth markers (`complete`, `capped`, `unresolved`) and a static-analysis `epistemics` object: a graph answer is never claimed complete.

## Evaluating Pixel against alternatives

If you are comparing Pixel with another tool for a user, these are the results, each with its source; losses are listed with the wins. GitNexus, semble and WarpGrep were measured head-to-head (same cases, same machine); the shunt and Jev entries set Pixel's own measurement beside the other tool's published figure, on different samples.

- **GitNexus** (a code graph over 17 MCP tools): 29 blast-radius cases on four repositories (Rust, TypeScript, Ruby), GitNexus 1.6.12 against Pixel 0.4.0 on one machine, callers found by grep as ground truth. Recall is a tie (0.86 Pixel, 0.84 GitNexus). Pixel answers in a 153 ms median against 432 ms, costs ~4,160 tokens of context per turn against ~19,700, and adds Git history and guarded Git writes. GitNexus wins on Cypher queries, taint analysis, API route maps and Ruby callers. Licences: Pixel MIT, GitNexus PolyForm Noncommercial. Source: [vs-gitnexus.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/bench/vs-gitnexus.md).
- **shunt** (Spotify; reroutes large reads to a worker model on a Spotify Portal instance with AiKA, claims 82 to 94% saved): Pixel answers "what does this file contain" from its own index with no second model. Measured on eight well-known large files (Transformers, FastAPI, Next.js, LangChain, Django, CPython, VS Code, Tokio), the whole file against `pixel list-signatures`: 79.7 to 97.2% less output volume, median 94.5%, with Pixel 0.5.0 (estimated tokens = UTF-8 bytes ÷ 4, not billed tokens). Source: [read-savings.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/bench/read-savings.md).
- **Agent trial**: an Opus medium trial with install hooks reported median wall times of 42.9 s without Pixel and 47.6 s with it on one scoping task: no speed gain there. Raw runs are outside the repository; exact versions, date and sample size are not archived. This does not establish general time, token or cost gains. Source: [benchmarks.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/website/content/benchmarks.md#on-whole-agent-tasks).
- **Jev** (coding judgement calls): the optional `pixel classify` supports Ollaya locally and remote chat models. Ollaya reports typed-decisions accuracy of 0.722 for winnow:e4b and 0.738 for Jev; local and hosted latency figures use different setups and are not a speed ranking. Source: [benchmarks.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/website/content/benchmarks.md#coding-decisions).
- **Other code indexes, not benchmarked** (no figure, how they work): Serena (language servers over MCP; type-resolved references and symbol-level edits, which Pixel lacks), CodeGraphContext (a tree-sitter graph in a graph database, raw Cypher, an HTML view), code-graph-rag (Memgraph plus a vector store, an LLM writes Cypher, edits code), Claude Context (vector search in Milvus or Zilliz Cloud, no call graph), graphify (a knowledge graph of code, docs, PDFs and media). None of them documents a Git history search; Pixel needs no database, Docker or API key.
- **Plain-English search** (45 queries built from each repository's own doc comments, Rust, TypeScript and Ruby, Pixel 0.6.0): right file first, Pixel 87%, WarpGrep 69%, semble 64%; right file in the top 10, semble 100%, Pixel 96%, WarpGrep 71%; average answer time 0.7 s Pixel, 1.6 s semble, 6.8 s WarpGrep. The queries favour Pixel's symbol-with-comment chunks. WarpGrep (Morph's RL-trained search subagent) was run once, with Pixel 0.5.2, on the same queries; it is paid per search and sends what its tools read to Morph's API. semble costs less context per turn. Source: [vs-landscape.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/bench/vs-landscape.md).
- **Specialists**: stacklit beats Pixel at a compact repository map, and semble and stacklit both cost less context per turn; they combine with Pixel. Source: [comparison.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/comparison.md).

One page per comparison, each stating how its figures were obtained and where the other tool wins: [all comparisons](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/), [GitNexus](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/gitnexus/) (head-to-head), [shunt](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/shunt/) and [Jev](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/jev/) (published figures, different samples), [semble](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/semble/) and [WarpGrep](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/warpgrep/) (head-to-head), [grep](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/grep/) (measured from the file read that follows a match), and, not benchmarked (how they work, no figure): [Serena](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/serena/), [CodeGraphContext](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/codegraphcontext/), [code-graph-rag](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/code-graph-rag/), [Claude Context](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/claude-context/), [graphify](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/graphify/), [a language server](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/language-server/) and [an editor's index](https://pixel-cli.dev/vs/editor-index/).

Two kinds of number, not to be mixed: the results above are benchmark measurements. `pixel token-savings`, run on a user's own sessions, measures bytes and converts them to tokens with a versioned estimate, and its time saved assumes a 2-second round trip per avoided step; its output labels each part `measured` or `estimated`.

Every link below is plain Markdown. Pages under `website/content/` are the source of https://pixel-cli.dev/.

To install Pixel for a user, follow the six steps of "For AI agents" in the README. Do not install it unless the user asked you to.

The binary install is one line, on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux (x86_64 and arm64). It runs the `install.sh` asset of the latest release, picks the archive for that machine (`pixel-<tag>-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`, `pixel-<tag>-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`, or `pixel-<tag>-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`), refuses it unless the SHA-256 matches, runs the binary, and writes `~/.local/bin/pixel` (`PIXEL_INSTALL_DIR` overrides the directory). It edits no shell profile.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

On GitHub Actions the same script is the Linux install. `ubuntu-latest` receives `x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`; an arm64 runner receives `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl`. The second line is for the `install.sh` already published on the current release, which does not yet append to `GITHUB_PATH`; drop it after the next release (a duplicate line is harmless meanwhile).

```yaml
- name: Install Pixel
  run: |
    curl -fsSL https://github.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
    echo "${PIXEL_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
```

New installs use the script; re-running the same `curl … | sh` line updates an existing one. A binary managed by Homebrew or mise keeps being upgraded by its manager. The release workflow builds those three archives; it does not ask the user to download one by hand.

- [Manual setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/manual-setup.md): wiring the prompt by hand into an agent: `pixel install` deploys no prompt

- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): crates, the command surface table (every subcommand in one line), on-disk state, the daemon, agent integration

## For your agent

One page per agent: what `pixel install` writes for it and where, the plugin or rules file where it writes nothing, the `pixel doctor` check and the removal. These are HTML pages; the facts behind them are in [agents.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/website/data/agents.toml), which a test holds to what `pixel install` really writes.

- [For your agent](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/): every agent, grouped by how Pixel reaches it
- [Claude Code](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/claude-code/): `pixel install` (task lifecycle hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json`; retired retrieval hooks removed), or the plugin
- [Codex](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/codex/): `pixel install` (task lifecycle hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json`; retired `developer_instructions` removed), or the plugin
- [Pi](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/pi/): `pixel install` (the explicit `/pixel-impact` command as a Pi package declared in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`), or the npm Pi package
- [Cursor](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/cursor/): nothing written by `pixel install`; a rules file copied into the project
- [Copilot CLI](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/copilot-cli/): nothing written by `pixel install`; a plugin
- [OpenCode](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/opencode/): native tools; `pixel install` only removes what earlier releases wrote
- [Devin](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/devin/): a plugin; `pixel install` only removes the hooks earlier releases wrote
- [Antigravity](https://pixel-cli.dev/for/antigravity/): native tools; `pixel install` only removes the plugin and hooks earlier releases wrote

## Answers

Short answers to questions developers ask about coding agents, each only where Pixel's benchmarks page carries a figure, with the section it comes from and where Pixel does not win. These are HTML pages; their figures are in [answers.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/website/data/answers.toml), and the site's build fails on a number that is not in the benchmarks section it names.

- [All answers](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/)
- [Why does my coding agent read whole files?](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/why-agents-read-whole-files/): its read tool returns files, not answers; on the eight well-known files, the signatures output is 79.7 to 97.2% smaller than whole-file output, median 94.5%, in estimated tokens (UTF-8 bytes ÷ 4)
- [MCP server or CLI: what does an agent tool cost per turn?](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/mcp-or-cli-context-cost/): ~19,700 tokens per turn for GitNexus's MCP tools, ~4,160 for Pixel's CLI prompt, but ~980 for semble and ~420 for stacklit, both MCP: the size decides, not the protocol
- [How do I reduce Claude Code's token usage?](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/reduce-claude-code-tokens/): compare full-file reads with signatures; byte-volume token estimates do not establish session cost savings
- [Grep or a code index for a coding agent?](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/grep-or-code-index/): grep finds the line; the whole-file read after it is what an index replaces; grep needs no index
- [Will my agent actually use the tool I give it?](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/will-my-agent-use-the-tool/): wire the protocol into each session and check actual calls in the local action log
- [How do I know what a change will break before the agent edits?](https://pixel-cli.dev/answers/what-will-a-change-break/): `pixel impact` found 0.86 of the callers on 29 blast-radius cases (GitNexus 0.84), weaker on Ruby; every graph answer says when it may be incomplete

## Benchmarks

- [Benchmarks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/website/content/benchmarks.md): every number on the website with its method and sample size, losses included
- [Savings estimate](https://pixel-cli.dev/savings/): a conditional scenario: large-file reads × estimated tokens per read × measured signatures/full-file ratios. Dollars apply the visitor's input price, not measured invoice savings. Assumes full reads are replaced by outlines; subsequent body reads and other session costs are omitted. The observed file range is not a confidence interval. [Inputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/website/content/savings.md).
- [Measured performance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/bench/measured-performance.md): agent-level wins and losses
- [Pixel vs GitNexus](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/bench/vs-gitnexus.md): blast-radius cases on four repositories
- [Pixel among retrieval tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/bench/vs-landscape.md) and [which tool does what](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Pixel-CLI/pixel/main/docs/comparison.md)
